title: Nalu
summary: An offline-first business assistant for a real artisan paleta business: purchases, sales, inventory by movement, profit with historical cost and reports that export to PDF or an image for WhatsApp.
role: Solo — product, frontend, API, data model and deployment.
context: A small reseller buys paletas from suppliers, sells at home or at a stand, and tracks stock between the two. The record usually lives in a notebook, which makes the two questions that matter — what do I have, and what did I actually earn — hard to answer after the fact.

solution.title: Inventory as signed movements
solution.body: Stock is derived from purchases, sales, gifts, own consumption and losses rather than edited directly. Every change has a reason and a history, so the available quantity can always be explained.

solution.title: Profit with historical cost
solution.body: Sales keep the cost that applied when the product was bought, so margin does not move retroactively when a supplier raises a price.

solution.title: Works without a connection
solution.body: Sales, purchases and stock movements are recorded locally first and synchronised through an outbox when the network returns. The app installs to the home screen and reports export as PDF or a branded image.

contribution: Solo project, built for a real business. I designed the data model, wrote the React client and the Express API, implemented the offline outbox and the reporting, and deployed it on Cloudflare Workers with D1.
approach: The app is deliberately a learning project with production habits: strict TypeScript, a shared Zod contract between client and server, tests on both sides and end-to-end tests for the flows that matter. The offline decision came from the setting — a stand with unreliable mobile data — and it changes the data model: a sale has to be valid before the server has seen it.

technicalDecisions.title: Movements, not a stock counter
technicalDecisions.body: A counter is one write and no explanation. Signed movements cost more rows and answer “why is it 12 and not 14”, which is the question the owner actually asks.

technicalDecisions.title: Outbox sync with explicit states
technicalDecisions.body: Writes are queued locally and retried; the interface shows whether a sale has reached the server. Silent failure would be worse than a visible delay in a shop.

outcomes: A sale can be recorded with no connection and reaches the server when the network returns.
Profit and margin are computed from historical cost instead of today's supplier price.
The business owner gets a report as an image that can be sent in the same chat the business already uses.
evidenceNote: Verified against the public nalu-app repository and its live deployment on 2026-11-25. No revenue, customer count or usage figure is published.
